newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AIG Hong Kong gold desk to shift to U.S. - traders.
newsitem.headline: AIG Hong Kong gold desk to shift to U.S. - traders.

text.p: AIG International Inc's gold trading desk in Hong Kong will shift its operations to the United States, most likely before the end of 1996, gold dealers said on Friday.
The change will involve transferring one dealer, currently based in Hong Kong, to the firm's headquarters in Connecticut, market sources said.
"They will do exactly the same thing (as in Hong Kong), only from the U.S.," said one gold dealer at a local bullion house who declined to be identified.
Traders said AIG will continue to cover Asian time zones in their entirety, and the change was merely a physical relocation.

"The dealer will just have to work the night shift, that's all," a senior Hong Kong gold trader said, noting that AIG's declining revenues in Hong Kong from a lacklustre gold market had prompted the decision.
AIG International is a unit of American International Group.
